grammar.ar: نسأل How often عن عدد المرات، ونجيب: once a week, twice a week, every day.

I play basketball once a week.
I run every day.

words.ex: My brother often plays games after school.
I play video games with my cousin.
My sister watches cartoons at the weekend.
At the weekend, I play video games.
The tablet has a big screen.
I turn off the TV at eight o'clock.

dialogue.t: Noura, how often do you play video games?
Only at the weekend, Mum.
Good. And your brother?
Omar often plays games after school.
Do you watch cartoons in the morning?
No, never. I go to school!
Ha ha. What time do you turn off the TV?

grammar.title: How often does he/she …? He often plays …
grammar.ar: مع he و she نستخدم does في السؤال ونضيف s للفعل في الجواب.
examples: How often does she watch cartoons?
She often watches cartoons.
He never plays games at night.

words.ex: My hobby is drawing.
I draw pictures of cars and camels.
I read comics every night.
Sam makes models of planes.
I draw three times a week.
In my free time, I read comics.

dialogue.t: Wow! Are these your models?
Yes! My hobby is making models.
How often do you make them?
Three times a week, after school.
What do you do in your free time?
I draw pictures of cars and camels.
Do you often read comics?

grammar.title: Time phrases at the end: … three times a week
grammar.ar: عبارات مثل once a week و every night تأتي في آخر الجملة.
examples: I make models three times a week.
She reads comics every night.
We draw pictures once a week.

words.ex: We go camping in the desert.
We eat out on Thursday night.

We sometimes have a barbecue on the roof.
We eat lunch together on Friday.

dialogue.t: Noura, what does your family do at the weekend?
We often go to the farm.
How often do you go camping?
Once a month, in winter. We go to the desert.
We usually eat out on Thursday night.
Do you have a barbecue?
Yes, sometimes, on the roof!

grammar.title: How often does your family …? / We + frequency word
grammar.ar: عن العائلة نقول we، وللسؤال: How often does your family …?
examples: How often does your family eat out?
We eat out once a month.
We often go to the farm.

Sure!
How often do you play football?
Every day, after school.
Do you often watch TV?
No, I never watch TV.
Thanks, Omar! Now I can tell the class.

grammar.title: Reporting a survey: He/She + frequency word + verb-s
grammar.ar: عند إخبار الصف عن صديقك نستخدم he/she والفعل مع s.
examples: He plays football every day.
She sometimes reads books.
Most of my friends never watch TV in the morning.

OK. And then?
Turn left. It's next to the art room.
Where's the canteen?
Go down the stairs and turn right.
Is it next to the office?

grammar.title: Imperatives: Go … / Turn …
grammar.ar: لإعطاء الاتجاهات نبدأ بالفعل مباشرة: Go, Turn, Walk.
examples: Go up the stairs.
Turn left.
It's next to the art room.

words.ex: The toy shop is between the shoe shop and the bookshop.
The toy shop is opposite the ice cream shop.

How do we get there?
Take the lift. Then turn right.
Look! There's the lift.
Good. Now go past the bookshop.
I can see it! It's opposite the ice cream shop.

grammar.title: Prepositions: between, opposite, next to
grammar.ar: between = بين شيئين، opposite = مقابل، next to = بجانب.
examples: The toy shop is between the shoe shop and the bookshop.
It's opposite the ice cream shop.
Go past the bookshop.

words.ex: Go straight on to the park.
Cross the road at the traffic lights.
Turn left at the traffic lights.
There's a shop on the corner.
My school is on a big street.

dialogue.t: Excuse me. Where's the park, please?
Go straight on. Then turn left at the traffic lights.

Then cross the road.

Which corner?

grammar.title: More imperatives: Go straight on. Cross … Don't …
grammar.ar: للنهي نقول Don't + الفعل: Don't cross here.
examples: Go straight on.
Cross the road at the traffic lights.
Don't turn left. Turn right.

words.ex: Reem is looking at the zoo map.
Walk along the path to the lake.

The café is in front of the monkeys.

Let's meet at the entrance at five.

dialogue.t: Where are the giraffes, Reem?
Look at the map. Walk along this path.
OK. And then?
Turn right. The giraffes are near the lake.
I'm hungry. Where's the café?
It's in front of the monkeys.
Is it far?

grammar.title: in front of / behind / near
grammar.ar: in front of = أمام، behind = خلف، near = قريب من.
examples: The café is in front of the monkeys.
The lions are behind the giraffes.
Walk along the path.

words.ex: Excuse me, where's the café?
How do I get to the gift shop?
The dinosaur room is at the end of the hall.
Take the stairs to the second floor.
The gift shop is near the entrance.

Take the stairs to the second floor.
The second floor. And then?
Turn left. It's at the end of the hall.
Excuse me again. How do I get to the gift shop?
It's on the ground floor, near the entrance.
Is it next to the café?

grammar.title: Asking the way: Excuse me, how do I get to …?
grammar.ar: للسؤال بأدب عن الطريق: Excuse me, how do I get to …? أو Where's …?
examples: Excuse me, how do I get to the café?
It's at the end of the hall.
Take the stairs to the second floor.

words.ex: First, go to the big tree.
Then turn right.
Our treasure is a box of chocolates.
Can you find my treasure?
The box is under the stone.
Go between the well and the tent.

dialogue.t: Can you find my treasure, Emma?
Yes! Where do I go?
First, go to the big tree.
OK, I'm at the tree. Then?
Good! Go between the well and the tent.
Is the treasure in the tent?
No. Look behind the tent, under the big stone.

grammar.title: Order: First … Then … + imperatives
grammar.ar: نرتّب الاتجاهات بـ First ثم Then ونبدأ بالفعل.
examples: First, go to the big tree.
Then turn right.
The treasure is under the stone.

Sure, Mum! What can I do?
Can you set the table?
Yes. How many people?
Can you pour the juice, please?
Sure. Orange or mango?
Mango, please.

grammar.title: Can you …? / Let me …
grammar.ar: لطلب المساعدة: Can you + فعل؟ ولعرضها: Let me + فعل.
examples: Can you help me, please?
Sure!
Let me wash the dishes.

words.ex: Could you help me, please?
I tidy up my room on Saturday.
Could you pick up your toys?
Put away your books, please.
I make my bed every morning.
Of course! Let me help you.

dialogue.t: Omar, your room is very messy!

Of course. Could you pick up your toys first?
OK. Where do they go?
Now could you make your bed?
Sorry, I can't. I don't know how.
Let me show you. Look!

grammar.title: Could you …, please? (polite)
grammar.ar: Could you أكثر أدباً من Can you، ونجيب: Of course أو Sorry, I can't.
examples: Could you pick up your toys, please?
Of course.
Sorry, I can't. I'm busy.

words.ex: Can I help with the bags, Dad?
Let me carry this big bag.
The water bottles are very heavy.
Ali opens the door for Dad.
Could you put the milk in the fridge?
Thanks, Faisal. That's kind.

dialogue.t: Hi, Dad! Can I help?
Yes, please. These bags are heavy.
Let me carry this big one.
Thanks, Faisal. That's kind.
Could you put the milk in the fridge?
Sure! Where do the eggs go?
In the fridge too, please.

grammar.title: Offering help: Can I help? / Let me …
grammar.ar: لعرض المساعدة: Can I help? أو Let me + فعل. والرد: Thanks, that's kind.
examples: Can I help?
Let me carry this bag.
Thanks, that's kind.

words.ex: Our guests today are Grandpa and Grandma.
Could you bring the dates, please?
Grandpa loves dates.
Dad makes the Arabic coffee.
Could you clean the small cups?
Reem welcomes the guests at the door.

dialogue.t: Reem, the guests are coming at four.
Can I help, Dad?
Yes. Could you bring the dates, please?
Of course. The big plate or the small plate?
Could you clean the small cups for the coffee?
Sure. Can I make the Arabic coffee too?
No, it's very hot. Let me make it.

grammar.title: Could you bring …? / Can I …?
grammar.ar: Could you للطلب بأدب، وCan I لعرض المساعدة أو الاستئذان.
examples: Could you bring the dates, please?
Can I help?
Let me put them on the table.

words.ex: Omar waters the plants on the roof.
Noura feeds the cat every morning.
Could you take out the rubbish, please?
Mum sweeps the kitchen floor.
Sorry, I'm busy. I'm doing my homework.
No problem, Mum! I can do it.

dialogue.t: Omar, could you water the plants on the roof?
No problem, Mum. I'm going now.
Noura, could you feed the cat?
Sure. Let me get her food.
OK. Omar, could you sweep the floor later?
Sure. Can Noura take out the rubbish?
OK, after my homework.

grammar.title: Saying no politely: Sorry, I can't. I'm …ing.
grammar.ar: للاعتذار بأدب: Sorry, I can't ثم السبب بصيغة ing.
examples: Could you water the plants? No problem!
Sorry, I can't. I'm doing my homework.
Let me feed the cat.

words.ex: We get ready for Eid at night.
Faisal decorates the living room.
Here are the red and green balloons.
Reem wraps presents for her cousins.
My job is to decorate the door.
Could you help me with the balloons?

dialogue.t: Eid is tomorrow! We need to get ready.
Can I decorate the living room?
Yes, please. Here are the balloons.
Let me help you, Faisal. I love balloons!
Of course. Who are the presents for?
For your cousins. Here's the paper.
Mum, can you help me? I can't reach the top.

grammar.title: Asking and offering: Could you …? / Let me …
grammar.ar: في التخطيط نطلب بـ Could you أو Can you، ونعرض بـ Let me أو I can.
examples: Could you wrap the presents?
Let me decorate the door.
I can carry the balloons, and you can wrap the presents.
